summary: SPOQ is a Claude Code-based multi-agent methodology: epics are decomposed into YAML tasks with explicit dependencies, dispatched in topological 'waves', gated by a 10-metric planning validation and a 10-metric code validation, with an optional human-as-agent in planning and a three-tier Opus/Sonnet/Haiku hierarchy. It is evaluated with synthetic DAG scheduling runs, four benchmark tasks (planning quality, validation ablation, human-assist), a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B replication, and an uncontrolled field log of 17 repositories.

claims.claim: Wave dispatch approaches the critical-path bound (CP ratio 1.03-1.11, up to 14.3x speedup) and gives ~1.4x on a 2-slot local backend.
claims.evidence: Table 5 (10 runs, synthetic sleep tasks) and Table 6 (Qwen, 2 slots). Numbers match the abstract. But the FIFO dependency-queue and role-based baselines are implemented to serialize execution (§6.3 'all three baselines serialize execution'), so the speedup is wave-parallel vs serial, not vs a competent parallel scheduler.

claims.claim: SPOQ planning raises coverage 93.0->99.75, removes cyclic plans, lifts parallelism 31.0->75.25.
claims.evidence: Table 7: 4 tasks, Claude 4 runs/task with sd; Qwen single run. Metrics are structural and partly rubric-scored ('Task estimates are inferred from task scope using the evaluator rubric'); the evaluator identity (human vs LLM) is not stated. Parallelism metric (share of zero-dependency tasks) is directly optimized by SPOQ's decomposition instructions.

claims.claim: Dual validation reduces defects 0.34->0.20/task and lifts test pass rate 91.25%->99.75%.
claims.evidence: Table 8 (4 tasks). Internal inconsistency: the same autonomous full-SPOQ pipeline on the same four tasks reports 0.47 defects and 96.50% pass rate in Table 10 ('Auto SPOQ'), larger than the gap the ablation attributes to validation. Qwen replication (Table 9) uses a different 0-100 'quality' scale and is single-run.

claims.claim: Human review reduces residual defects 0.47->0.03 per task.
claims.evidence: Table 10, 4 tasks; human is presumably an author; no blinding; LOC churn rises 5.75->104.25.

claims.claim: Longitudinal study (17 repos, 8,589 commits, 13,866 tests, 99.87% pass) provides ecological validation.
claims.evidence: §6.7.2 numbers present, but authors state no control group and reliance on reviewer-agent/self-reported confidence; 7,907 of 8,589 commits come from one adopter repo (speedrun-gitlab, Adrata). A test pass-rate snapshot does not measure SPOQ's effect. Case-study speedups are vs estimated sequential hours.

patterns.note: Epic->task->wave planner/executor hierarchy; evidence limited to 4 tasks.
Role tiers (Opus workers, Sonnet reviewers, Haiku investigators).
Parallel agents per wave; paper itself reports build-dir corruption, test-fixture invalidation and node_modules conflicts (Appendix B.5).
Post-execution code validation gate; ablation numbers internally inconsistent with Exp 4.
Sonnet reviewer agents score QA; field metrics rely on these scores.
Human-as-agent planning review lowers defects in Table 10, weakly (n=4, unblinded).
Cost tiering by model; no ablation of tiering itself.
Task YAML with acceptance criteria and files_to_touch.
Requirement files -> epics is spec-first in spirit, not evaluated as such.

methodology.sample: Exp1: 5 synthetic DAGs x 10 seeds; Exp2-4: 4 benchmark tasks (SaaS, e-commerce, chat, data/Terraform); Claude rows 4 runs/task, Qwen 1 run/task; field: 17 repos, uncontrolled.
methodology.baselines: Serial schedulers (strawman for parallelism); 'baseline Claude Code planning' with same requirements; no comparison to other multi-agent frameworks (MetaGPT, ChatDev) despite discussing them.
methodology.models: Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku via Claude Code; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B via llama.cpp.
methodology.variance: sd over 4 runs for Claude; none for Qwen; no significance tests.
methodology.ablations: Validation-gate ablation (none / code-only / full); human vs auto.
methodology.languages: Not specified for benchmarks; field includes Spring Boot API, Terraform, web callers.

standards.artifacts: Text says benchmark tasks and evaluator instructions are 'provided in the accompanying Git repository' but no URL is given in the paper.

biases.detail: Exp1 FIFO dependency queue and role pipeline are implemented to serialize; any parallel DAG scheduler would match SPOQ.
Authors' methodology, authors' rubric and metrics; the 'external client' case study (Pinpoint) is the authors' own affiliated company.
Field 99.87% test pass rate and agent confidence 0.90-0.95 do not measure SPOQ's causal effect; case-study speedups are against estimated, not measured, sequential durations.
Evaluator for defects/granularity is unspecified; Qwen evaluator scores 0-100 'quality'; field QA relies on reviewer-agent scores.
Full SPOQ defects 0.20 / pass 99.75% (Table 8) vs Auto SPOQ 0.47 / 96.50% (Table 10) on the same four tasks and pipeline.
No repository URL for SPOQ or benchmarks.
Abstract says the Qwen replication 'verifies' gains are orchestration-attributable from single-run, rescaled results.

coi.affiliations: Both authors list Pinpoint Technologies LLC (author emails at gmail and testwithpinpoint.com).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: SPOQ (authors' own methodology); Case Study 2 is a Pinpoint website rebrand labelled 'external'. Acknowledgments thank Adrata CEO whose repo dominates the field statistics.
coi.detail: Not a model vendor, but authors evaluate their own methodology with their own rubric on tasks they wrote, and present work on their own company's site as external field evidence.

verdict_reason: Useful, concrete design (dependency-wave dispatch, pre/post gates, human planning review, failure-mode catalogue in Appendix B.5) but the quantitative evidence is thin (4 tasks), uses serial strawman schedulers, has an unexplained Table 8 vs Table 10 inconsistency, unspecified evaluators, no released artifacts, and self-evaluation. Treat as a practitioner design report, not as evidence of effect size.
applicability: For the Java team the transferable parts are design patterns rather than numbers: (a) task YAML with explicit dependencies and files_to_touch is a lightweight spec-driven unit that can be shared across hosts because it lives in the repo; (b) a planning-validation gate before execution maps well to spec review in spec-driven development; (c) the failure catalogue (shared build dirs like target/ corrupted by concurrent builds, test fixtures invalidated by sibling agents) is directly relevant to running parallel agents over several repositories — use per-agent worktrees and sequential cross-wave builds. SPOQ is single-repo epic oriented and tied to Claude Code tiers; it does not address cross-repo contracts for ingestion-to-delivery APIs, and its human-gate benefit is not measured in a regulated (the domain) review context.

conflicts_with.detail: SPOQ claims reviewer/validation interventions improve outcomes; Ada finds an LLM coach-judge injected into the agent loop extended runs and lowered judged conclusion grounding (GPT-4.1, 24 runs). Different tasks (code generation vs code understanding), so tension rather than direct contradiction.
